chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who was sick during the month of Ramadan, and when he recovered he intended to perform Hajj, how should he deal with making up the fasts? He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he returns, let him fast them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up Ramadan fasts if one intends to perform Hajj first?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the sequence of obligations for one who was ill during Ramadan, ruling that Hajj takes precedence over making up missed fasts (qada). This reflects the Shia scholarly view that while both are obligatory, the time-sensitive nature of Hajj allows it to be performed before the makeup fasts, provided the fasts are completed subsequently. The ruling underscores the flexibility in fulfilling deferred duties without invalidating the primary pilgrimage.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Hilal, from Uqba Bin Khalid,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who is sick during a Month of Ramazan. So when he gets cured, he intends the Hakk. How should he deal with the making up for the (missed) Fasts?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When he returns, so let him Fast them’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Hilal from ‘Uqbah ibn Khalid who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about a man who becomes ill in the month of Ramadan. When he becomes well he decides to perform Hajj. What is he required to do about Qada’ (compensatory fast) of the fast? He (the Imam) said, ‘When he comes back he must do its Qada’ (compensatory fast).’
